v: Beloved, let’s love one another, for love is of God; and everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.
b: This verse reminds us how great God's love is. This love exists not only in God's nature but also among us. It is a love that goes beyond oneself, cares for others, and is willing to give for others. And this love comes from God; it is one of the fruits given by the Holy Spirit in our hearts.

Our Jesus Christ is the greatest example of love. He gave His life for sinners and became our atoning sacrifice. His love is selfless and sincere; He forgave those in distress and let them feel God's love and grace. In the same way, in our daily lives we should strive to show this kind of love, especially to those who need help.

I remember a story. One day a young man passed a construction site and saw a bricklayer working with trembling hands. He asked, “What’s the matter with you?” The bricklayer answered, “My hand hurts a lot, and I still have to work for several hours.” The young man stopped and watched for a while, then asked, “Why don’t you take leave and see a doctor?” The bricklayer answered, “I need this job; I can’t quit over a small ailment.”

The young man was deeply moved. He decided to stay and help the bricklayer finish his work. Although he had no construction experience, he gave all his time and effort, helping the bricklayer carry heavy loads and speeding up the project. In the end the young man received the bricklayer's gratitude, and from him came to understand God's love.

This story tells us that in our lives each of us can show God's love by giving care and helping others. Do not pursue your own gain and comfort, but be willing to give for those around you who need help. Doing so not only helps others, but also makes us holier and more blessed.

In our daily lives, let us often ask the Holy Spirit to give us abundant love, and have the courage to act and show God's love. Let us strive to follow the example of the Lord Jesus, caring for others' needs and showing God's love and goodness, becoming a gospel light that enjoys God's favor.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May God's love be with you. Amen!

v: We know and have believed the love which God has for us. God is love, and he who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him.
b: This passage tells us that love is not only God's nature but also a gift He wants to give us. If we are to live in God, we must live in love. This is not only a guide but also a calling. People are often troubled by fear, worry and anger, but in God's love we can find rest and joy.

In the Bible there is a story of a lost son returning home. When the father saw his son coming, he ran to him, embraced him, kissed him, and ordered the servants to prepare a feast for him. This father's actions show God's love: even if we go far from Him on the wrong path, He waits for us to turn back, and welcomes us back into His arms.
In the same way, when we live in God's love, we can experience its power and victory, because God's love is boundless, unchanging and true, and able to defeat every form of sin and fear.

So how do we abide in love? We need to keep our relationship with God, obey His will, and continually ask Him for guidance and strength. In addition, we should show love and care to the people around us, and influence and change their lives in positive ways.
pr: Lord, lead us to abide in love, and make us instruments that show God's love to the people around us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May the Lord give you the grace and peace of being with Him, and may we all love others with God's love and influence the world. Amen!

v: For this is loving God, that we keep his commandments. His commandments are not grievous.
b: This verse calls us to keep God's commandments, because this is loving God. Sometimes we may think that keeping God's commandments is hard, but this verse tells us that in fact God's commandments are not burdensome. Why? Because God left His commandments to us to help us know His heart and bring us closer to Him.

In our lives we often meet all kinds of difficulties and challenges. With God's commandments we have a guiding lamp and know how to walk the road of life. It is like an ant in the story that found a single straw in the wilderness, because it knew that on this grassland only that straw could guide it back to its nest. Although the many straws looked alike, only that special straw was the true way out.
In the same way, we too need to keep God's commandments and look for that true road. Even when we are lost or weary, God's commandments are still a bright lamp.
Let us remember that keeping God's commandments is not only our love for God but also our love for ourselves. For God's commandments are to protect us and make our lives fuller and richer.

Thank the Lord that we have His commandments to guide us, so that we can draw closer to Him and closer to our goals. May the Lord bless you, making your direction clear on life's road and making you His faithful servant. Amen!

v: Beloved, let’s love one another, for love is of God; and everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.
b: This passage tells us that true love comes from God, and only by building a good relationship with God can we truly experience selfless love. God's love is our source, and loving one another is also what Christians ought to do.

A husband and wife had a great rift between them because of a quarrel. Neither would yield, and neither wanted to apologize first. Later they attended a church gathering and received this advice from an elder: “Do you love your spouse? Then put down your own pride and pay attention to the other’s needs.”
The elder's words inspired the couple, and after careful thought they finally apologized to each other and began to pay attention to each other's needs. Their love was reborn because of it.
In the same way, in our relationship with God, if like this couple we focus only on our own needs and not on God's, our faith will be drained away.

So we should strive to build a good relationship with God, and strengthen our faith through prayer, Bible reading and fellowship with other Christians. At the same time, we should love one another, pay attention to the needs of others, and give them real support and encouragement.
Let us remember that only love that comes from God can truly become the source of love, and loving one another is also an important part of the Christian life.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience love from God and true happiness in your relationships with God and with others. Amen!

v: We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. He who doesn’t love his brother remains in death.
b: This verse reminds all of us who believe that love is a very important element; it not only brings joy and happiness but can also affect our spirit and spiritual growth. Like a doctor, if he has no love, his duty is merely to cure the patient's bodily illness, without any healing of the heart. In the same way, if we do not hold an attitude of love toward the people around us, our actions may even hurt their hearts.

When we love our brothers and sisters, we not only strengthen trust and relationships with each other, but our souls are also lifted up. Let us illustrate this with an example. Suppose someone who had lost himself, after a long time, found the Lord and found himself again, and was successfully freed from sin and found a new purpose in life. When he meets those who once treated him badly, if he still holds a grudge, then his life has not truly changed. But if he can treat those who once hurt him with love, then his soul can truly be set free and healed.

This also fits the teaching of Jesus Christ, who said: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” (Matthew 22:39) This teaching tells us that love is selfless giving; through love we can think of others and care about their needs and feelings. Just as we eat food every day, we also need to “feed” our souls in daily life and treat ourselves and those around us well, because this kind of love not only brings us hope and comfort in our hearts, but also lets us see God's grace and blessing.
pr: God, You have given the grace of love. Make us channels that pass on love, to help those who need love and attention, so that they too can experience God's goodness and blessing. May we, through the power of love, pass out of death into life and enjoy abundant life.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you be full of God's love and grace. Amen!

v: He who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, for God is love.
b: Dear brothers and sisters, in our lives love is a very important power. This is what God's holy word tells us. Only when we have love can we truly know God; only through love can we deeply experience God's lovingkindness and grace. So what is love? Perhaps we can learn from a true and moving story.

The story is about a woman who suddenly suffered a stroke. Her family and the doctors did everything they could to save her, but in the end it was in vain. Her young daughter took her mother's body to an organ donation center, because she knew this was what her mother had wanted to do while alive. In the end her mother's organs saved several lives; this was the comfort the daughter felt in her heart when she lost her mother, and also the continuation of her mother's life.

This story tells us that the power of love is endless. The daughter deeply loved her mother, and even though she was gone, she still wanted to use her mother's organs to continue life and bring others hope. In the same way, when we have true love, we too can bring hope and life to others.

This reminds me of a passage in the Bible: “This is my commandment, that you love one another, even as I have loved you.” (John 15:12) This is God's command, and also God's lovingkindness to us. When we love others as Christ did, we can truly know God, because God is love.

Let us remember this truth at all times in our lives, and let love be the standard of our conduct. When we face adversity and setbacks in life, let us look at others with love, and face everything in life with God's love. For only through love can we truly know God, and in our lives love is a priceless treasure that can bring us endless strength and hope.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you have abundant love in your life, love others as Jesus did, become a child of God, and enjoy His grace and lovingkindness. Amen!

v: Even as the Father has loved me, I also have loved you. Remain in my love.
b: This passage reminds us that the Lord Jesus' love for us is as vast as the Father's love for Him. In the way the Bible describes it, from the whole universe down to the capillaries of every blade of grass and the veins of every leaf, the love of the Lord Jesus fills everything. So we are told to remain in His love.

There is a story of a young man who took part in a marathon. At the start he was very excited and enthusiastic, but after a few kilometers he began to feel tired and weak. At that moment he saw an old man sitting by the roadside, holding a bottle of water and waving to him. The young man felt it was strange, but still ran over and took the bottle the old man held out. After a few mouthfuls of water, his strength and spirit were restored, and he went on to finish the race.

This illustration tells us that on the road of life we also face weariness, setbacks and difficulties. We need, like the young man, to meet God's love and grace on the road. When we feel weary in our faith, we need to keep returning to God's love and let His grace nourish our souls.

Through this passage we know that the love of the Lord Jesus is boundless; it can heal our hearts and inspire us to go on. Wherever we are, we can find quiet rest in the Lord's love and receive the Lord's guidance and help. Let us remain in the Lord's love, make this love the most important thing in our lives, and in continual pursuit become Christians who are full of love, faith and hope, like the Lord Jesus.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you remain in the Lord's love on the road of life, receive His guidance and help, and pursue His will with faith, hope and love. Amen!

v: If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, even as I have kept my Father’s commandments and remain in his love.
b: Through this verse God tells us that obeying His commands in love is very important. For when we obey God's commands, we not only experience His love, but also receive His care and protection. It is like when parents tell a child to do something: if the child listens and does it, the parents are very happy, and give the child more love and attention.

In life we also need to obey God's commands. Doing so may not always be the easiest thing, but it is well worth it. There is an inspiring story about obedience that is worth learning from and thinking over. It is about a top athlete who took part in a very important race. His coach told him he must carry out the set plan, and he listened to the coach's instructions. In the race he felt great pain and exhaustion, but he persisted in following the coach's instructions. In the end he overcame his exhaustion and pain and won the race. This story tells us that when we trust God and obey His commands, even in the face of hardship and challenge, we can overcome them and gain victory.
Let us obey God's commands and act in love. When we do this, we can receive abundant grace and blessing in His love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you all. May you keep obeying God's commands and act in love, and receive His protection and care. Amen!

v: I made known to them your name, and will make it known; that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.”
b: This verse tells us that the Lord Jesus not only died for our sins, but also to lead us into His love.

A young man fell into deep depression after his father died. He kept asking himself, “Where is my father? Does he still love me?” He felt very lonely and helpless, until one day he dreamed that his father came and shook his hand and said to him, “Always remember, wherever and whenever, I will be in your heart.” This made the young man feel very comforted and encouraged, because now he knew that his father was in his heart forever, loving him.

In the same way, we too can receive such great love, because the Lord Jesus has shown us His love. This love is not only His sacrifice on the cross for us, but also includes His making His name known to us, so that we can know of His existence and love. When we receive the Lord Jesus' love and let Him into our hearts, we too can experience His presence and grace.

So let us remind ourselves and others every day that the Lord Jesus' love always exists and never changes. Let us be like that young man, remembering His love wherever and whenever, because His love will remain in our hearts forever. In the name of the Lord Jesus I bless you: may you experience His love, faith and hope every day. Amen!

v: may be strengthened to comprehend with all the saints what is the width and length and height and depth,
b: How wondrous and magnificent is the love of Christ! In this world, the love we see and hear about is often selfish, given in hope of a return or to meet our own needs. But the love of Christ is completely selfless. He gave His own life to save us, asking nothing in return, so that we could be with God forever. How vast and deep such love is!

There is a story about a mother's love. One day a little boy accidentally fell into the water. He struggled desperately but could not swim to shore. When his mother saw it, she jumped in without regard for her own safety and rescued her son. This mother's love reminds us of God's love for us. He, too, did not count His own safety, and did not hesitate to give His own life to redeem us.

May we, like the saints, understand how wide and long and high and deep the love of Christ is, and may we love others as He did: selflessly, generously, and sacrificially. Let us use this sincere love to reveal God's glory and make this world a better and warmer place.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you feel Christ's boundless love and grace at every moment along the road of life, and may you give your life to pass on and share God's love. May your life be full of faith, hope, and love. Amen!

v: I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. That life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me.
b: This verse tells us that as Christians, our life springs from faith in God's Son, Jesus Christ. Christ not only loves me, He gave Himself up for us. What profound love this is!
There is a story about a mother's love for her son. One day her son became ill and was hospitalized, needing a painful treatment. When the child was afraid, his mother decided to stay with him.

In the treatment room the child cried in pain, but his mother never left his side. She held his hand and said gently, "Dear, Mommy is here. Don't be afraid. I will be with you all the way, to support you and take care of you." Hearing his mother's words, the child gradually calmed down, because he knew his mother loved him.

This story reminds us that just as that mother treated her son, God treats us. God's love is unconditional, and that love made Him willing to give Himself up for us. God has not abandoned us. He is willing to accompany us personally as we face the difficulties and challenges of life.

In our daily lives we may also meet setbacks and difficulties. But when we trust in God and believe in His love and promises, we find that He gives us strength and courage to face everything. As the verse says, we live by faith in the Son of God, and the Lord Jesus is our hope and salvation.
In our lives, when we feel lonely, afraid, or disappointed, let us not forget that God is the source of limitless love. He gave Himself up for us, and He will be with us forever.
Let us rely on this love every day and live out the love of Christ with firm resolve.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God's endless love and strength every day. Amen!

v: and to know Christ’s love which surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
b: This passage tells us that God's love is beyond what anyone can measure. With human wisdom and strength we cannot grasp how deep, how wide, and how high God's love is. Yet God's love not only surpasses understanding, it also fills us. How great and how holy such love is!

A young man, crushed by the pressures of life, had a breakdown and fell into a pit of despair. He gave up on himself and even considered ending his life, but at his lowest moment he met a Christian. With care and patience, this Christian walked beside him through the dark time, and eventually his life was made new. The young man deeply experienced how immeasurable God's love is, and he thanked God for sending that Christian to help him.

God's love is shown not only in our lives but in many examples in the Bible. For instance, John 3:16 says, "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life." God gave His Son to us to save our souls. What abundant grace and love! Likewise, Romans 5:8 says, "But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us." Christ died for our sins entirely out of God's infinite love and grace.

This lets us feel how deep and rich God's love is! The love God gives us surpasses human ability, and even human longing and need. So we should always seek that love beyond measure, let it fill our lives, become children of God, and share this love with those around us.

Let us put this love into practice in daily life and show God's great love at every opportunity. As Matthew 5:14 says, "You are the light of the world." Let us shine brightly in our lives, lighting up those around us, so they can see God's immeasurable love and grace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May God's love and peace fill your heart, so that every day you can show forth God's great love. Amen!

v: nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
b: This verse lets us know that no matter how many hardships and challenges we meet, God's love will never leave us. This love is not based on our conduct but is established in our Lord Christ Jesus. It is like the love between a child and his parents: no matter how many mistakes the child makes, the parents' love does not change.

Yet sometimes we feel shut out of God's love by our own actions or those of others, and we feel lonely and lost. I remember a young girl who once told me her troubles. She had done poorly on an exam and felt very guilty and disappointed, and she felt that God no longer loved her. But I told her that God's love is not built on our performance, but on God's love and grace toward us. Through prayer and reading Scripture we can find spiritual comfort and strength, and build our faith on God's promises.

At the same time, we need to learn how to pass on God's love in daily life. There is a story of a young man walking on the beach with his friend, who saw the beach covered with stranded starfish. The young man began picking them up one by one and throwing them back into the sea. His friend asked what difference it could make, since there were so many starfish on the beach and he could never save them all. The young man answered, "At least I can help the ones I save. Every starfish I throw back shows love and care for this world."

Like this young man, even if we cannot help everyone in need, we can help those around us and pass on God's love and care. One small act can have a great effect, just as saving one starfish may change that starfish's whole life.
Let us remember that God's love cannot be severed. Whatever setbacks and challenges we meet, we can trust in God's love and grace. And we can also change this world by passing on God's love and care.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you become a person who passes on love in this world, and may God's love be shown in this world through your actions and words. Amen!

v: Now I beg you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, that you strive together with me in your prayers to God for me,
b: This passage reminds us that God's love is shown to us through the Holy Spirit. The Spirit's love is selfless and asks nothing in return. Like the wind, He always blows through our lives and guides us onto the right path.

The Spirit's love can also be shown through other people. Let me tell you a story. A man was waiting in a hospital for surgery, feeling afraid and alone. Just then a nurse came into his room. She said nothing, but sat quietly by his bed, held his hand, and gave him care and comfort when he needed it. Even after the surgery, she often came to his bedside to visit him and make sure his recovery was going well. This is the Spirit's love shown through a person.

We can also show the Spirit's love through our own actions. Once a mother took her little daughter to play at the park, and the girl began playing with a lonely little girl. This child said her mother had left her. The mother was very saddened, so she decided to show the Spirit's love through action. She invited the little girl to lunch, played games with her, and stayed with her until her father came to pick her up. All of this was inspired by the Spirit's love, a love like a warm wind that keeps encouraging us to help those in need.

Now let us pray for ourselves and for those around us. Let us join our hearts with the Holy Spirit and pray to the Heavenly Father. At this moment, let us pray for peace and blessing for those who need the Spirit's love and help, especially those around us. And let us remember that in all our actions and conduct we must show the love of the Spirit. May we all become a force of encouragement and help to others, and may the Spirit's love flow in our lives.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you enjoy God's grace in the love of the Spirit, and may you show the Spirit's love through action in your life, helping those in need. May you feel the Spirit's guidance and comfort at all times. Amen!

v: who also declared to us your love in the Spirit.
b: Dear friends, let us reflect together on the message of this verse. What is "love in the Spirit"? In the Bible, the Spirit's love comes from God. It is a selfless, sacrificial, gentle, and forbearing love. It does not belong to the selfish love of the world, but is given to us by God so that we may love and care for one another. This love not only joins us to God, it also joins us to others.

The Bible teaches us to love our neighbors, as Jesus said, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself" (Luke 10:27). There is an inspiring story about a young man named Xiaohua. After his mother died, he was often alone, sunk in sorrow. He felt that the people around him no longer cared about him, until one day a stranger saw his sadness on the street, came up and spoke with him, and gave him a warm hug and encouragement. This made Xiaohua feel he was no longer alone, and he regained confidence and love.

This story tells us that when we turn our eyes to others and care about their needs, we find that we ourselves benefit too. The Spirit's love is a selfless love. It makes us willing to help others, and willing to sacrifice our time and energy to care for them. As the Bible says, "Let all that you do be done in love" (1 Corinthians 16:14).

So let us ask God to give us the love of the Spirit and make us channels of His love, passing it on to those who need help. Like that stranger, let us be willing to go out and care for others, so that they may feel God's love and warmth.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you all. May God's Holy Spirit fill you and give you a selfless, gentle, and forbearing heart of love. Amen!

v: and hope doesn’t disappoint us, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.
b: Have you ever felt lonely, lost, and helpless? Perhaps you have done a great deal and given a great deal, but when you feel that those you love have not returned it, you feel uneasy and lost. When we are in such a situation, what we need is hope and love.

In the Bible, God gives us many teachings about love. His love is deeper than we can imagine. He died for us and sent the Holy Spirit to pour God's love into our hearts. When we receive His love, we can experience true freedom and peace.

There was a boy named John who lost his father when he was young. His mother worked very hard to support him. But through it all he felt very lonely and lost, and he thought everyone had left him. He began searching for a true home, longing for love and care. He investigated many different religions and beliefs, but never found real satisfaction.

Then one day he met a Christian family. This family taught him about love in the Bible and the work of the Holy Spirit. He began to understand that God's love could fill the loneliness and loss in his heart. Through his relationship with God, he felt completely accepted and loved. Today he has become a loving Christian, full of hope and faith, and he knows he will never be alone again.

God's love, through the work of the Holy Spirit, can be poured into our hearts and bring us true hope and comfort. When we feel lost and lonely, let us turn our eyes to God, and He will satisfy the longing of our hearts like a clear stream.
Thank You, Lord, for giving us Your love and the Holy Spirit to pour into our hearts, so that we can find true satisfaction and peace in You.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. I hope you will experience the presence of the Holy Spirit in your heart and the love of God, and find true hope and comfort in Him. Amen!

v: Put on therefore, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility, and perseverance;
b: In this verse God tells us that as His chosen ones, we are all beloved. Because God loves us, He chose us and made us His children. As beloved ones, how should we live? This verse tells us we should have a heart of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.

Think about it: if everyone had a heart of compassion, this world would have more care and sympathy. When we see others in trouble, we should not sneer at them or treat them coldly, but have compassion and care for them and help them. We should also have kindness, treating others as God does, not quick to anger and not willing to hurt others.

Next, this verse also speaks of humility, gentleness, and patience. A humble person never looks down on others or boasts; instead, they respect others and make room for different opinions and views. The same is true of a gentle person, who does not use power to suppress others but expresses their thoughts and opinions in a soft way. Finally, we need patience, because we will always meet many challenges and difficulties in life. Only people with patience can hold firm to their convictions, keep moving forward, and overcome obstacles.

A young man, in his college years, ran into many difficulties through his club activities and began to lose confidence. But he always remembered something a teacher once said to him: "You are loved by God, and He believes you can overcome everything." Those words rekindled his confidence in life and the future. He began to face challenges actively, and in the end he walked the road he had set his heart on.

We too are loved by God, and He believes we can overcome all difficulties and challenges. As long as we have hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience, we can become truly beloved ones. For such people give off God's love and light in their lives, lighting up the people and things around them and becoming a beautiful testimony.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May each of us become beloved ones, holding hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience, showing God's love and light, and filling this world with hope and joy. Amen!

v: Those who have believing masters, let them not despise them because they are brothers, but rather let them serve them, because those who partake of the benefit are believing and beloved. Teach and exhort these things.
b: This verse speaks of how we as Christians should treat one another. We have a believing master, and we should respect and serve him, and we should not despise other brothers and sisters either. For the benefit we finally receive is that we are believing and beloved. This is the motivation and goal of Christian action.

Timothy was a young pastor who met difficulties in his work. He did his best, yet always felt his strength was not enough and he needed more help. He had friends who cared for him, but they perhaps differed in their views on how to serve God and people.

At this time Timothy recalled the teachings of Scripture and the words of God, and with the help of the Holy Spirit he gained more wisdom and strength to carry out his work. He realized that only by practicing in faith could he truly help people. For those who partake of the benefit of service are precisely the believing and beloved.

At the same time, this passage also raises an important idea: we must not fail to respect one another just because we are brothers and sisters. Even when we have different views or methods, we should still treat one another with love. Only so can we show Christ's love and truth in our own lives.
Let us practice our faith every day, respect one another, and treat one another with love, so that we can serve God and people better.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you gain more strength and wisdom in faith, and treat those around you with love. Amen!

v: But God, being rich in mercy, for his great love with which he loved us,
b: This verse tells us how great and rich God's love is. His love is not only unique, but selfless and full of mercy. Like a father, His love goes beyond all understanding and bounds. God's great love knows no race, language, or background; it embraces everyone.

A couple met each other through a social platform. At their first meeting, the woman discovered that the man was disabled and could not take care of himself. But she did not give up on the relationship; she chose to give more love and care. She was not afraid of difficulties and challenges, but used her love and support to help him overcome one obstacle after another. This is the true meaning of love.

God's love for us is like that woman's. He sees our weaknesses and flaws, yet never gives up on us, and instead gives us endless grace and mercy. God's love is selfless, and He was willing to sacrifice Himself to bring us redemption and salvation. How great and abundant this is! At the same time, we should learn to love others, whatever their background or difficulties, using our care and support to help them out of hardship, loving and supporting one another.
Let us feel God's love in our daily lives, and love well those around us. For God's great love is with us, giving us faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May we keep pursuing the way of love, help one another, and receive more grace and mercy in God's love. Amen!

v: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the assembly and gave himself up for her,
b: We all know that marriage is a gift from God and one of the most beautiful experiences of our lives. But as couples, we often meet all kinds of difficulties and challenges. Sometimes quarrels, misunderstandings, even betrayal leave us feeling disappointed, discouraged, and helpless. But as the Bible says, we husbands are to love our wives, and this is not only respect and care for her, but obedience to God and faith in Him.

In this world, many couples part and divorce because they do not understand or tolerate one another. But if we can give ourselves up for our spouse as Christ loved the church, we can build a strong marriage. In the Bible, Christ gave Himself up for the church and gave His life in exchange for our redemption. This is the most perfect expression of love.

There was a young couple who felt exhausted by financial pressure and the pressures of life, and their marriage began to have problems. But they decided to face these challenges together, supporting each other with love and faith. In the end they got through the hard times and built an even stronger marriage. This is the power and blessing that self-giving love can bring.

Let us keep in mind the Bible's teaching: love is the cornerstone of a strong marriage. If we are willing to bear with and support one another, we can overcome every difficulty and challenge with the power of love. Let us love our spouses with a self-giving attitude, as Christ loved the church, and believe that God will keep and bless our marriage until eternity.
dc:
In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May the Lord bless you and keep you; may the Lord make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you; may the Lord lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.
Amen!

v: For the love of Christ compels us; because we judge thus: that one died for all, therefore all died.
b: This passage reminds us how greatly Christ's love compels us. Christ paid the price of death for us, and this selfless, sacrificial love should become the motivation and inspiration of our lives.

In life we often meet setbacks and difficulties. Sometimes we feel powerless and think we cannot go on. But let us remember that Christ's love compels us. He gave Himself up for us and bore all our sins and pain. His love is so great, so unconditional, so endless. When we feel we lack strength, we can turn to this love and gain strength and courage from it.

A young man met with many setbacks and failures in life and felt he had nothing. Then one day he met an old man. The old man told him, "Do you know that a God named Jesus loves you, and He gave Himself up for you? His love is so strong and so deep that He is willing to give everything for you." The young man felt Christ's love, and his life was encouraged. He began to face life's challenges again and to meet the future with faith and hope.

Dear family, let us also be like this young man and find strength and motivation in Christ's love. When we meet difficulties and setbacks, remember that He gave up everything for us, and this love can inspire us to persevere. Whether at work, at home, or in school, let this love be our motivation, so that we can go beyond ourselves and pursue a better future.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you deeply feel every day that Christ's love compels you, bringing you faith, hope, and love. Amen!

v: My love to all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.
b: In this passage we see that God conveys a very important message to us: His love is with us. What grace this is! Through Christ we can experience God's immeasurably rich love, a love that goes beyond all we can understand.

In our daily lives we may face all kinds of troubles and challenges. Sometimes we may feel lonely and helpless, even fall into despair. But we must remember that whatever situation we are in, God's love is always with us. He never forsakes us; He is always by our side.
A young man named Xiaoming had a very big dream: to become an excellent musician. But he was mocked and discouraged by people who said he would never achieve this dream.

Facing this pressure and difficulty, Xiaoming did not give up. Every day he studied and practiced hard, and firmly believed that God would help him achieve his dream. Finally one day he got a chance to show his talent in an important music competition.

In this competition, Xiaoming played with all his heart, showing the effort and perseverance he had put in over many years. In the end he won the championship and became a musician whom everyone admired.

This story tells us that even in adversity, as long as we hold fast to our convictions and believe that God's love is with us, we can overcome every difficulty. Like Xiaoming, his faith and perseverance finally helped him achieve his dream.

So when we face challenges in life, let us not be discouraged or give up, but believe that God's love is with us. He will give us strength and wisdom to overcome every difficulty and achieve our dreams.

Finally, let us bless you in the name of the Lord: may you deeply experience God's love and presence every day, and firmly believe that He will lead you through every difficulty and help you achieve your dream. Amen!

t: Through the One Who Loved Me
v: No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.
b: In our lives we often meet all kinds of challenges and difficulties that leave us feeling helpless and at a loss. Yet when we rely on the Lord who loves us, we can be more than conquerors in all these things.

A young man grew up in poverty, and his family's finances were very hard. He worked hard every day, but his income was never enough to live on. This left him feeling desperate and helpless, and he thought he would never escape poverty.

But he did not give up. He knew he needed to rely on a greater power. He began to learn to trust in God and often prayed for help. This changed his outlook, and he began to believe he could overcome in the midst of difficulty.
One day he met a wealthy merchant who saw his effort and perseverance and decided to give him a chance. The merchant invited Xiaoming to join his company and gave him good work and a good salary.

The young man was filled with gratitude and was deeply moved. He knew that all of this was a gift of God's grace and love. He understood that it was through a heart that loves the Lord that he had gained victory and overcome the limits of poverty.

In our lives we also face all kinds of difficulties and challenges. But as the Bible says, through the Lord who loves us, we are more than conquerors in all these things. When we place all our faith and hope in the Lord Jesus Christ, His love and power will fill our lives and lead us out of hardship.

Let us live a victorious life every day with a heart that loves the Lord. Whatever difficulties we face, let us firmly believe that God's love and grace are enough to sustain us and make us more than conquerors.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you gain victory in faith, hope, and love. Amen!

v: But now faith, hope, and love remain—these three. The greatest of these is love.
b: In this passage, God teaches us the importance of love. Faith and hope are certainly important, but love is the most important element of all. Love is not just a feeling; it is an action, a power that changes the world. There was a young girl named Lily, and in her school there was a classmate named Emma, a hearing-impaired student. Emma often felt lonely and excluded because she could not communicate with others as easily as other students. But Lily saw Emma's inner beauty and potential. She decided to spend time learning sign language and took the initiative to talk with Emma. This giving and caring made Emma feel accepted and loved, and her life changed from then on.

This story tells us that love is not just saying "I love you" with the mouth; what matters more is showing it through action. Love is paying attention to others' needs, and being willing to give time and energy to care for, encourage, and support others. When we treat others with love, we not only change their lives, we also feel great joy and fulfillment.

In our daily lives, we can apply this idea in every area. Whether with family, friends, coworkers, or strangers, let us keep a heart of love at all times. When we treat others with love, we are also showing God's love, because God is love itself.

Dear family, let us remember every day that the greatest is love. Wherever we are, whatever difficulties we face, let us meet them with love and kind conduct. May we bring faith to everyone who falls into despair, give hope to everyone longing for hope, and pass on God's love to everyone who needs love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you become a witness of love, bringing hope, joy, and lovingkindness to everyone around you. Amen!

v: But the goal of this command is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith,
b: In this passage, God reminds us that the goal of His commands is love. Love is a strong and powerful force. It can change hearts, inspire people, and bring us faith, hope, and love.

In a school in a small town, a teacher cared deeply for his students, especially those who were not doing well. One year there was a student named Xiaohua whose grades were never good and who easily got into conflicts with classmates. The teacher decided to use love to change Xiaohua's life.

After school every day the teacher stayed behind to help Xiaohua review his lessons, giving him encouragement and guidance. Not only that, the teacher wrote a letter to Xiaohua's parents, telling them that their son had great potential and needed only a little love and support. Seeing the teacher's concern for Xiaohua, the parents also began to take a more active part in their child's education.

Slowly, Xiaohua began to feel the love of his teacher and family. He began to study hard, broke his bad habits, and got along well with his classmates. His grades improved noticeably, and he became more confident and optimistic.

This story tells us that love is a powerful force that can change a person's life. When we treat others with love, we not only bring them hope and confidence, we also inspire them to love, care for, and support others.
May God's love fill each of our hearts, so that we treat others with love and care for and help one another. May you find true peace and joy in love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you grow strong in love. Amen!

v: Love doesn’t harm a neighbor. Love therefore is the fulfillment of the law.
b: In today's world we often see many forms of violence and harm. This grieves us deeply, because it is not God's will. God wants us to live out the spirit of love, caring for, cherishing, and respecting one another.

A movie star, a man full of love and kindness who often helped others, received a letter one day. The letter said, "Your performance makes me jealous and full of hatred. I will find a chance to make you pay!" He was very shocked, but he did not take revenge. Instead, he chose to respond with love.

He began to pay attention to this person and took the initiative to look for chances to help him. He did not blame or hurt him, but brought him warmth and care. Gradually this person's heart began to change; he realized his wrong behavior and felt true love and forgiveness. In the end they became friends and worked together on many meaningful things.

This story tells us that when we face hatred and harm, we can choose to respond with love. Love can change others, and it can also change us. When we live out the spirit of love, we can build true relationships and make peace and harmony a reality.
So let us ask ourselves every day: How do we treat others? Do we treat them with love? Let us remember that love does no harm to a neighbor, and that love is the fulfillment of the law.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you live out the spirit of love every day and show God's love to others. Amen!

v: However, if you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well.
b: In our lives we sometimes easily overlook the importance of loving others as ourselves. We often pursue our own interests and forget to care about the needs of others. But God calls us to keep this royal law in full, and that is truly good.

I would like to tell a story to inspire us, about a young boy. One day he saw an old man fall down in the street. Other people just hurried past, and no one stopped to help him. The boy was moved with compassion and ran to the old man without hesitation, helped him up, and asked whether he needed help. The old man nodded gratefully and told the boy he needed to be taken home. The boy walked the old man back to his home and even helped him tidy up the room. As they said goodbye, the old man looked at the boy with deep feeling and said, "Thank you. Your kindness made me feel warm and cared for." The boy was very happy and fulfilled to hear this, because he knew he had kept God's law and shown love to another.

This story tells us that loving others as ourselves is not just a slogan but an action. Like that boy, when we see someone in need, we should reach out a helping hand without hesitation. Whether in our families, communities, or workplaces, we can show love and care through small acts.

Dear family, may we remember this royal law at all times and love others as ourselves, because this is what God asks of us. When we keep this law in full, we will be witnesses of the light, bringing faith, hope, and love to this world.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep growing on the road of loving others as yourself and become a person who truly cares for and loves others. Amen!

v: Owe no one anything, except to love one another; for he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.
b: In this passage, God reminds us that love for others is very important. We are called to love one another, and to remember always that our love for one another is a lifelong debt. When we treat others with love, we keep God's law and fulfill what He asks of us.

A little boy named Peter was often laughed at by his classmates at school because he had a disabled leg. He often felt inferior and lonely, unable to find a place where he belonged. But one day a classmate named Emily came to him and showed him true love and care. She not only became Peter's good friend, she also encouraged him to join the school sports competition, and always supported him when he needed help. Emily's love let Peter feel God's love for him and changed his life.

This story tells us that when we treat others with love, we can bring them real change and hope. We are not just individuals; we are connected to others on a shared journey. God calls us to love one another not only because we have a responsibility to each other, but because in loving one another we can feel God's endless love and grace.

So let us act in love every day, not only in words but in deeds. When we see someone in need, let us not hold back from reaching out a hand, giving them love and care. Such love not only fulfills the law, it also brings us peace and joy.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May God bless you, and as you give love, may you also feel His boundless love. Amen!

v: But anyone who loves God is known by him.
b: In this passage we learn the importance of loving God. Love is the key to building a deep relationship with God. When we truly love God, God also watches over us and builds a close relationship with us. A young man named Arthur was, in the eyes of his family, a complete failure. He was often late and lazy, and seemed cold and unfeeling toward others. But at one opportunity he met a kind teacher, who not only encouraged him but gave him love and care. This love changed Arthur. He began to study hard and to be kinder to others. In the end he became an outstanding professional and influenced many more people with his love and care.

This story reminds us that love is a powerful force. When we treat others with love, we can change their lives, and we change ourselves as well. Love is a gift God has given us, and we should make good use of this gift to pass on warmth and hope to those around us.

Let us treat others with love every day, whether family, friends, or strangers, because love can connect people to one another. When we learn to love God, we will also receive God's love and blessing.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you grow strong in love and become a person who pleases God. Amen!

v: No one has seen God at any time. If we love one another, God remains in us, and his love has been perfected in us.
b: This passage reminds us that although we cannot see God with our own eyes, if we love one another, God lives in our hearts, and His love can be perfected in us. What a wonderful truth! Through loving one another, we can experience God's existence and His perfect love.

There was a young girl named Lily. At school she met a classmate who was very hard to get along with, who often bullied her and other children and left them feeling helpless and hurt. Although Lily was hurt, she did not retaliate or strike back, but chose to respond with love.

Every day Lily cared for this classmate, took the initiative to chat with her, and helped her solve her problems. She never held the girl's bad behavior against her, but treated her with love and care. Gradually this classmate began to feel Lily's love and concern, and the wall of ice in her heart slowly melted away.

This story tells us that when we love one another, we can influence others and change their hearts. Whether in family, work, school, or community, we have chances to show God's love and become a light in someone else's life.

We can take inspiration from Lily's example: whatever difficulties or challenges we meet, we can choose to respond with love. When we look at others with love, it is as though God lives in us and His love is perfected in us. Such love can change hearts in a miraculous way and bring harmony and joy.

Let us work every day to love one another, whether toward family, friends, coworkers, or strangers. Such love can cross boundaries and create a beautiful, peaceful environment. May you experience God's presence and perfect love as you love one another.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you become a witness of love, leading others onto the right path and finding strength and hope in love. Amen!

v: whom, not having known, you love. In him, though now you don’t see him, yet believing, you rejoice greatly with joy that is unspeakable and full of glory,
b: This passage reminds us of an inspiring story. In it there is a young man named David who was visually impaired. Although he could not see the beauty of the world, he had a heart that loved music. He was full of passion for music and dreamed of becoming a pianist.

Although David had never seen a sheet of music, he believed in his own ability and persevered. He began to practice by listening to music and imitating the sounds of the piano, and also learned piano techniques from others. His patience and perseverance moved many people, and they gave him support and encouragement.

Finally, David showed his talent in an important music competition. As he sat before the piano and his fingers lightly touched the keys, everyone was stunned by his beautiful playing. Without a word, David's music conveyed an incomparable joy and hope.

We can find inspiration in David's story. Although he had never seen a sheet of music, David believed in his own ability and kept pursuing his dream. In the same way, our love for the Lord is built on faith and hope. Even though we have never seen Him with our own eyes, we can love Him through faith and through obedience to His word.

Such love can let us experience joy unspeakable, and can also inspire us to strive for spiritual growth and goals in our lives. Just as David showed his talent in the music competition, we too can pass on hope and joy to the world through the love and faith we show for the Lord.

So let us love the Lord every day with faith and hope, and boldly pursue our dreams and spiritual growth. Believing in God's existence and His love for us, we can go beyond our limits and show His wonderful work in our lives.
dc:
In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you have endless joy and hope in love, and may you experience in faith the satisfaction and peace God gives. Amen!
(The closing remarks already run about a minute and a half; please adjust as you see fit.)

t: If Anyone Does Not Love the Lord
v: If any man doesn’t love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be cursed. Come, Lord!
b: Dear friends, this passage reminds us how important it is to love the Lord, for if anyone does not love the Lord, they will be under a curse. This is a sobering truth, but it is also an alarm that can awaken us. Let us consider a question: do we love the Lord with all our heart and strength?

In life, love is a motivation and a power. A young man named David came from a poor family, but he had a heart full of faith, hope, and love. Despite all kinds of hardships and challenges, he never gave up his love for God. At work, in school, and in his dealings with others, David always faced things with an attitude of love. This love changed not only himself but the people around him.

As the verse says, if we do not love the Lord, we may fall into a curse and into trouble. But when we love the Lord with a loving heart, we will welcome the Lord's presence and blessing. This love brings not only personal blessing, but also sows seeds of hope and love in our families, workplaces, and communities.

So today let us reconsider whether our love for the Lord is enough, and whether we love Him with all our heart and strength. Following David's example, let us love the Lord with faith, hope, and love, and show true Christian character in daily life and in our dealings with others.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your love be deeply rooted in the Lord Jesus Christ, and may you, like David, be a blessing to others. Amen!

v: Let brotherly love continue.
b: In this busy world we often overlook the importance of building sincere relationships with others. God calls us to keep a heart of brotherly love at all times. This is a selfless love that is not limited to our own family or circle of friends but extends to all our brothers and sisters.

Imagine a small village where people love one another and care for one another. They share each other's joys and sorrows and help one another through difficulties. This village became a warm place full of love, because everyone put love at the center.

Like the village in this story, we too can show a heart of brotherly love in our lives. When we see someone in need, we do not offer only words of blessing but care for them through practical action. A greeting, a smile, a caring word can let people feel God's love and our concern.

We can also find many stories and parables about love in the Bible. For example, in the Gospel of Luke, Jesus tells the parable of the Samaritan. When the Samaritan met a man who had been robbed and badly wounded, he not only stopped to help, but also took care of him and paid his medical expenses. This parable tells us that love is selfless, that it crosses race, social status, and background, and that it binds us together.

Let us put love at the center of our lives and love one another. When we begin from love in how we treat others, we will see miracles happen. We will feel God's presence and become channels of His love, bringing faith, hope, and love to others.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God's endless love and grace every day. Amen!

v: having heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and of the love which you have toward all the saints,
b: This passage reminds us of two important things: faith and love. Our faith comes from Christ Jesus, who is the foundation and support of our lives. When we believe in Him firmly, we can experience God's power and grace.

But faith is not merely a theoretical idea; it should also be shown in our conduct. This is the "love toward all the saints" mentioned in the verse. It is a selfless, compassionate, and caring love. When we live out such love in Christ, we can support one another, grow together, and witness God's love flowing among us.

A Christian named Danny often saw a sick brother named Peter at church. Every time he saw Peter, he would go over to care for him, greet him, and pray for him. Danny did not stop at words of concern; he put sincere action behind them, helping Peter with his daily needs, such as buying food or accompanying him to the hospital.

This kind of love not only let Peter feel God's love and care, it also inspired other believers to be more active in service. This story tells us that our love has the power to change lives. When we are willing to give ourselves and help others, we can become vessels of God, and also plant seeds of hope and joy in the lives of others.

So on our journey of faith, let us not only have strong faith but also keep love for others. Whether in the family, the church, or the community, let us treat others with love, care for one another, support one another, and be witnesses of God.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you stand firm in faith and serve others with love. May your life become a source of blessing and hope. Amen!

v: The second is like this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
b: Love is a holy power that can change our lives and the lives of others. When God created us, He gave us the ability to love, so that we could care for and love one another. Yet this world is often filled with selfishness and hatred, and we often overlook the importance of loving others as ourselves.

Abraham Lincoln once told a story that can help us understand what it means to love others as ourselves. Once, in a small town, he met a wounded soldier whose leg was badly injured and who could not walk. Lincoln did not hesitate; he picked up the soldier and carried him with great effort for two blocks until he found a hospital. His action showed the spirit of loving others as oneself: he was willing to give others the help they needed, even at great cost.

This reminds us of the teaching of our Lord Jesus Christ. He tells us that only when we put ourselves in others' places and experience the troubles and sufferings they go through can we truly understand what loving others as ourselves means. It means not just words of blessing, but putting love into practice, caring for, helping, and supporting those who need help.

Let us ask ourselves: do we treat others with the same love every day? Or are we more inclined to be self-centered, caring only about our own interests and needs? Loving others as ourselves is not easy, but if we take Christ's love as our example and keep a heart of gratitude and humility at all times, we can do it.

Loving others as ourselves is not a doctrine that stays within the church walls but a practice that can be woven into our daily lives. When we see someone in need, let us not stand by but reach out to help. When we are with others, let us pay attention to their feelings and needs. When we face difficulties and challenges, let us respond with kindness and love. In this way we can be witnesses of love and sow the seeds of God's love in this world.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep growing on the road of loving others as yourself, extending your love and care to others. May you experience God's abundant love every day and share that love with others. Amen!

v: He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself.”
b: In this passage, Jesus teaches us to love God with all our heart and to love our neighbor as ourselves. This is a commandment about love, and it is God's call to us.
Love is a power that can change people's lives and even change a whole society. Let us hear an inspiring story about how one person changed his community by loving his neighbor as himself.

Once there was a small town whose people were always suspicious of one another and did not trust each other. Everyone cared only about their own interests, and no one was willing to help others. Such a community was full of coldness and division.
But one day a young man moved to this town. His name was Aaron. Aaron was a believer, and he firmly believed that God's love can change everything.

Aaron began a project. Every week he held a community gathering in his front yard and invited all the neighbors. He provided food and drink and created a warm and friendly atmosphere. At these gatherings people began to talk with one another and share their worries and joys.

Aaron also took the initiative to help neighbors in need, whether repairing a house, shopping, or watching children, and he reached out a hand without hesitation. This act of love was contagious, and slowly others also began to care for and help one another, forming a community full of love.

This story tells us that only when we treat our neighbors with love can we create a harmonious society. Love builds connections between people and breaks down division and indifference. When we love our neighbor as ourselves, we will be willing to sacrifice our own interests, care about the needs of others, and help them with practical action.

Aaron changed his community with an attitude of loving his neighbor as himself, which is exactly what God calls us to do. Let each of us become an Aaron and use the power of love to change the places where we live.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you treat your neighbors with love and become a witness who brings others faith, hope, and love. Amen!

v: Don’t forget to show hospitality to strangers, for in doing so, some have entertained angels without knowing it.
b: In this verse we are reminded to welcome strangers with love. Doing so is not only a way of showing love and kindness to others, but also holds a wonderful possibility: we may entertain angels without knowing it.

An elderly couple lived on the edge of a small town. One day a stranger appeared at their door, looking tired and hungry. The couple did not know who this stranger was, but with loving hearts they welcomed Him at once. They invited Him in, gave Him a good meal, and offered Him a comfortable place to rest. When the stranger left, the couple felt very happy and fulfilled, because they knew they had done the right thing. Not long afterward, the stranger revealed His true identity: He was an angel whom God had sent to test people's love and kindness.

This story tells us that when we welcome others with love, we may in fact be welcoming angels. We cannot know the story and wonder behind each person, but we can choose to treat them with love. Sometimes we may meet difficulty, pressure, or weariness, but when we choose to treat people with love, we can plant seeds in each other's lives and bring change.

So let us ask ourselves every day: Do I treat strangers with love? Am I willing to entertain angels without knowing it? Let us remember that everyone we meet may be an angel in disguise, and that through our love and care we have the chance to give them the power to change.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you show selfless love every time you welcome others, bringing them faith, hope, and love. Amen!

t: A Love That Lays Down Life
v: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.
b: This passage reminds us of God's definition of love and calls us to witness to His grace with self-giving love. In this world we see many forms of love, but the greatest is being able to give oneself up for one's friends. This selfless love surpasses all others.

Speaking of self-giving love, I am reminded of a moving story. A young doctor gave up a prosperous medical career and went to serve in a small village in a poor region. The people there suffered greatly from a lack of basic medical facilities.

This doctor spared no effort in providing medical care to the villagers, even sacrificing his own health and personal time. He built a medical center in the village and organized a team of volunteers, bringing health and hope to the community.

This story tells us that love is an action. It is not merely an expression in words but requires action and devotion. As we know, the Lord Jesus Christ sacrificed His own life on the cross to save us from the cost of sin. His self-giving love is the cornerstone of our faith.

In daily life we too can serve others with the same love. This may mean giving material help to those in need, offering inspiration and encouragement, or simply listening to someone's story with caring eyes. When we treat others with love, we not only bring them hope and happiness, but also show forth God's love.
Let us reflect every day on God's selfless love for us, and draw strength from this truth full of faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you show the power of love in your own actions and pass this love on to the people around you. Amen!

v: and in godliness, brotherly affection; and in brotherly affection, love.
b: This passage tells us that the journey of faith is not only about building a close relationship with God but also about showing sincere love for His people and for the world. Godliness is our connection with God, and love is our connection with others.

In a small village there was a young shepherd named Jonathan. Every day he took his flock out to graze, and he was full of love for every sheep in it. He always tended them carefully, making sure they had plenty of food and clean water. Jonathan knew that only by caring for the flock with all his heart could he become a worthy shepherd.

But one day Jonathan met a challenge. He found a little lamb trapped in a deep pit, unable to save itself. The rest of the flock watched from nearby, as if waiting for Jonathan to act. Jonathan realized at once that he needed to show a love beyond his love for the flock, and to have a heart of love for everyone.

He decided to risk danger to rescue the lamb. Jonathan jumped into the pit, and it took him a long time to get it out. When he lifted the little lamb, the rest of the flock cheered, as if they knew Jonathan had taken a risk to save a weak one. This story reminds us that to love our brothers and sisters means not only caring about their spiritual needs but also paying attention to their problems and troubles in life.

Back in our own lives, we too face many opportunities to show love for everyone. Perhaps someone around you needs help and care, or someone in your circle of friends needs sincere listening and support. We can show God's love by caring about others' needs and helping them.

Let us begin to strengthen our love for our brothers and sisters and for those around us. When we care for them with godliness and keep increasing our love for them, we will be God's witnesses in the world. For love can change hearts and bring hope and peace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find true joy and fulfillment in love. Amen!

v: But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting nothing back; and your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High; for he is kind toward the unthankful and evil.
b: This verse tells us an important truth: love is a power that overcomes everything. Sometimes we meet enemies, or are treated coldly and unfairly, and our instinctive reaction may be to take revenge or protect ourselves. Yet God asks us to respond with love.

Loving our enemies and being kind to them is very hard to do on our own. But this is exactly the likeness of the children God wants us to be, and it can be done only by God's grace. God is kind to the ungrateful and the wicked, and we too should learn how to show such love.

There was a young man named Peter who was bullied by a classmate for a long time. This classmate often mocked Peter and even hurt him. Yet Peter did not take revenge; instead he showed this classmate concern and friendship.

Peter knew that this classmate's home situation was not good, and that he was always in a state of pain and unease. So Peter decided to use love to change this classmate's life. He began to talk with him and gave him support and encouragement. Gradually the classmate's attitude began to change. He no longer bullied Peter, and instead became Peter's good friend.

This story tells us that when we face our enemies with love, we can change the course of events. When we choose to be kind to them and lend to them expecting nothing in return, we show God's grace and glory. Such love not only brings us a greater reward, it also makes us children of the Most High.

Let us act this way in our lives too. Perhaps someone has treated you unfairly or hurt you, but do not take revenge. Instead, respond with love. This love is the way to show forth God's grace and glory, and it is the proof that we are children of the Most High.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you treat your enemies with love and lend expecting nothing in return. May your life show forth God's grace and glory. Amen!

v: Even so husbands also ought to love their own wives as their own bodies. He who loves his own wife loves himself.
b: This passage reminds us that as husbands, we should treat our wives with the same love. Just as we take care of our own bodies, we should care for, cherish, and love our wives.

We can find inspiration in the story of a young husband. This husband, whom we will call John, was a busy engineer. He worked long hours every day and came home exhausted. Yet he always gave his wife the warmest love and care.

One day his wife became ill and needed rest and care. John took several days off and cared for his wife with all his heart. He cooked, did laundry, cleaned, and even watched movies and read with his wife. Although he had many things to deal with, he always put his wife's needs first.

This story tells us that John understood how a husband should cherish his wife. He did not just say he loved her; he expressed his love through action. He was willing to give time and energy to make sure his wife felt loved and valued.

This also reminds us that love is a selfless giving, not just an expression in words. When we truly cherish our wives, we will take the initiative to care about her needs and be willing to sacrifice our own comfort and interests.

At the same time, this passage also challenges us. As husbands, we should keep pursuing the perfection of love. We should learn to be understanding, respectful, and tolerant toward our wives. We can ask ourselves: Am I truly taking good care of my wife? Do I put her needs first?
Let us remember the message of this passage and put it into practice in our lives. Let us love our wives with the same love, so that we can truly experience the fullness and happiness God gives us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God's grace and blessing in your marriage. Amen!

t: The One Who Loves the Lord
v: One who has my commandments and keeps them, that person is one who loves me. One who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him, and will reveal myself to him.”
b: The word "love" always sounds warm and tender to us, but love is not only a feeling; it is the power of action, a power that changes the world. In this passage God tells us that the way to love the Lord is to keep His commandments, because such a person truly loves the Lord.

So what does it mean to keep God's commandments? Here we can use an inspiring story to illustrate. There was a young man named Enoch who longed to become an excellent basketball player. But he found that his height was not enough to compete with other players, so he made a decision: no matter what, he would work hard to follow his coach's instructions and do special training and conditioning every day. After a long period of effort, Enoch became the steadiest rebounder on the team, with outstanding skills and a strong body that went beyond his height. This is the power of love and obedience.

In the same way, when we keep God's commandments, we are also showing our love for Him. By humbly submitting to God's will, we experience His love and grace. Like Enoch, we must hold to God's commandments every day, never treating any bit of them lightly or neglecting them. Such a way of life will bring us closer to God and win His delight. In this love God also reveals Himself to us, letting us feel His presence and support.

So let us take love as our motivation, keep God's commandments, and bring love to this world. In daily life we may meet many difficulties and challenges, but when we act in love we can change hearts and bring hope and encouragement to others. Like that basketball player who worked hard to follow instructions, in our lives such effort and devotion will surely show forth God's love and grace.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience His love and grace as you keep God's commandments. May your life become a witness. Amen!

v: Love is patient and is kind. Love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud,
b: This passage tells us that love is not only a feeling but an action. Love is a posture of patient endurance: whatever difficulties and challenges it faces, love always holds on. Love is also an attitude full of kindness, willing to give and to care about the needs of others.

Here Paul also says that love does not envy. Envy is a negative emotion; when others get what we long for, we may feel envious. But true love does not let envy occupy the heart, because love is selfless. Love is not for its own interests but for the happiness of others. Love is glad to see others succeed and finds joy in their success.

A young man named Deming and his best friend Xinhua took the college entrance exam together. They both hoped to be admitted to the same school and spend their college years together. But when the results came out, only Xinhua was admitted, and Deming was not.

At that moment Deming felt envy rising in his heart. As he watched Xinhua happily preparing for college life, he could not help feeling lost and envious. But Deming decided to face his envy. He chose to bless Xinhua and hoped he would have a wonderful time at college. Deming worked to cultivate patience and the character of love that does not envy.

The story did not end there. A few years later, Deming found an ideal job at a large company and received an unexpected opportunity for promotion. His effort and perseverance were rewarded, and his attitude was changed too.
This story tells us that when we can overcome our envy and bless others with a heart of love, we open a window and let blessings and good things flow to those around us.

So in our daily lives, let us keep the attitude of a love that does not envy, bless others, and be willing to share in the joy and success of others. Such love will bring us the power of faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience patience and kindness in love, for love does not envy. May you see others through the eyes of love and find joy and success in blessing. Amen!

v: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will be done away with. Where there are various languages, they will cease. Where there is knowledge, it will be done away with.
b: In this verse Paul reminds us that love is an enduring power that always exists and always has value. Other abilities and knowledge may cease, but love is eternal.

Imagine a person in the dark of night who has lost his way and feels fear and despair. Suddenly a beam of light shines ahead of him, bringing warmth and hope. That is the power of love; it can light up the darkest corners of our lives.

We live in a world full of strife and hatred, where people are often self-centered and overlook one another's needs and feelings. But when we treat others with love, we can change this world. Like a flower in bloom, love gives off its fragrance and draws the butterflies and bees of thriving life. Our love can also draw those who are hurt and need comfort, giving them hope and strength.

We can express love in many ways, such as caring about the needs of others, helping the vulnerable, and giving encouragement and support. Just as Jesus Christ showed love with His own life, we too can show the true meaning of love in our lives through selfless devotion and giving.

There is a story about a young man's good deed. Every day he went to a nursing home to keep company with the lonely elderly. He shared stories with them, listened to their hearts, and gave them love and companionship. With his time and care, this young man lit up the lives of those elders and let them feel the warmth and presence of love.

For each of us, this story is a reminder that whether in the family, the workplace, or the community, we all have the chance to be bearers of love. Whatever difficulties or challenges we meet, let us look at others with eyes of love and respond with good deeds and compassion.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God's endless love every day and become a witness of love. May your life be like that beam of light, lighting up those around you and bringing them faith, hope, and love. Amen!

v: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
b: In this verse we see the difference between knowledge and love. Knowledge can make us feel proud, thinking we know more and are more important than others. But such an attitude only creates a gap between us and others and keeps us from building real relationships.
