By contrast, love is a power that builds people up. When we treat others with love, we can truly pay attention to their needs, be willing to give to help them grow, and be willing to touch their hearts. Love can change not only ourselves but also have a profound influence on others.

There was a young man who was very intelligent and had a wealth of knowledge. But he always looked at others with a sense of superiority and was unwilling to cooperate or learn with others. Later he met a teacher with a kind heart and selfless love. The teacher was willing not only to listen to the young man's confusion and challenges, but also guided and encouraged him patiently. Gradually the young man came to understand that real growth depends not only on knowledge but also needs the nourishment and guidance of love. He learned to treat others with love, care about their needs, and share his knowledge and experience. In the end he not only grew himself but was also able to help others onto the road to success.

Dear family, let us understand that no matter how much knowledge we have, if we have no love, all that knowledge is in vain. Only when we treat others with love, care about their needs, and are willing to help them grow can we truly build people up and bring them faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you treat others with love every day and become a guide in their lives. Amen!

v: If I speak with the languages of men and of angels, but don’t have love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.
b: This verse reminds us that even if we have many talents and can speak beautiful words or do amazing deeds, if we have no love, it is all empty.

We are often attracted by the outward success that society pursues, chasing fame, wealth, and power. But what God asks of us is not only outward achievement; He cares more about the state of our hearts. He cares whether we have love and whether we treat others with love.
Many times we easily overlook the importance of love.

There was a young man who was very successful in his career and had much wealth and fame. Yet inside he felt empty and lonely. He always put work first and neglected communication and love with his family and friends.

One day he met an elderly neighbor who lived alone nearby. The man began to talk with him, help him, and share his time and love. Gradually they built a deep friendship, and the man also came to experience the power of love.
The man understood that true success is not only achievement in one's career but also includes care and love for others. He began to readjust the focus of his life and put love first.

Dear family, in daily life let us remember: "Without love, we are like a sounding gong or a clanging cymbal." Wherever we are and whatever work we do, let us treat others with love. Let us learn to care for those around us, give sincere love, and support and encourage one another.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: "May all that you do be done in love. Amen!"

v: If I have the gift of prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but don’t have love, I am nothing.
b: This passage reminds us that ability, knowledge, and faith are not enough; without love, all of it is meaningless. Love is the cornerstone of our dealings with people and the bond that connects us to God.

There was a lonely old man who had no family and no friends, and lived a lonely, solitary life every day. One day a young man passed by his door, saw the old man's loneliness, and stopped to chat with him. They talked for a long time, and the old man began to feel the warmth of love. He knew he was not alone, that someone was willing to keep him company. This simple act changed the old man's life, and he began to find hope and joy in life again.

This story tells us that the power of love is limitless. Each of us can be like that young man and pass love on to those around us who need it. Perhaps just a smile or a caring greeting can light up someone's life. Whatever the size of our abilities, as long as we act in love, we can become God's instruments and bring hope and love to this world.

Let us examine ourselves every day and ask whether we are truly living out love. Let us not focus only on our achievements and abilities and overlook love. If we have no love, everything is empty. Let us put love first and weave love into our lives, so that others see God's love shown through our actions and attitudes.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you live out the value of love every day and become a light and hope in the lives of others. Amen!

v: If I give away all my goods to feed the poor, and if I give my body to be burned, but don’t have love, it profits me nothing.
b: This passage reminds us of the importance of love. People may give a great deal in pursuit of fame and wealth, but without love all of it is empty. There was a rich merchant with great wealth and position, respected in society. Yet inside he felt lonely and empty. One day he met a destitute orphan, whose face was haggard and whose clothes were ragged. The merchant was deeply touched by the orphan's eyes and decided to help and care for him. He provided food, clothing, and educational opportunities, and gave him love and care. As time went by, the orphan became happy and confident, and achieved success.

This story tells us that even the richest and most powerful people in the world, if they lack love, find their wealth and status to be of no profit. What truly has value is putting love into action and helping those who need help.

In our lives, perhaps we are not rich or powerful, but everyone has the chance to show love. Whether caring for a tired coworker, helping a stranger, or giving time to a community in need, every small act of love can change someone's life.
Let us take love as our foundation and influence the world with charity and care. As Paul says in 1 Corinthians, without love we are nothing.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you live out the truth of love every day and be a blessing in the lives of others. Amen!

t: Who Can Separate Us from Love?
v: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Could oppression, or anguish, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?
b: In life we sometimes face all kinds of difficulties and challenges, and these situations may leave us feeling lonely and helpless. Yet this verse reminds us that no difficulty or adversity can separate us from the love of Christ. Even in the hardest moments, God's love is still with us.

There was a young woman named Lily. Lily met with many difficulties: family problems, financial pressure, and health problems kept coming to her. But Lily did not give up. She held on to her belief that God's love and His plan for her had a greater meaning.

Every morning Lily read the Bible and prayed, and felt God's presence and comfort. She experienced miracles and grace on the journey with God. Once, at her most difficult time, she met a stranger who offered her a job and helped her solve her financial problems. Lily deeply experienced that God cares not only about her spiritual life but also about her daily life.
This story tells us that even when we are in trouble, God's love and His help are always with us. We can trust in Him, knowing that He will provide help and shelter when we need it most.

So whatever difficulty or challenge we face, let us keep this in mind: no difficulty can separate us from the love of Christ. When we feel lonely or helpless, we need only turn to God, and He will give us strength and comfort.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you deeply experience God's love and His hope for you in every circumstance. Amen!

v: Therefore I beg you to confirm your love toward him.
b: In this passage Paul urges us to show steadfast love. This is a thought-provoking message, because in life we often meet many difficulties and challenges that test our love. Yet God asks us to hold on to steadfast love, showing it in good times and in hard times alike.

There was a young girl named Mary. She lived in a poor neighborhood, but she always helped those in need with a loving heart. Even though she had difficulties of her own, she still made time and energy to care for others. Every day after school she went to the nearby neighborhood to help look after elderly people living alone at home. She talked with them, kept them company, and gave them love and care. Mary understood that love knows no rich or poor and no age, and that as long as we are willing to care for others with a loving heart, we can become vessels of God, passing on His love.

In life we also meet difficulties and many setbacks. Sometimes we may feel tired and helpless, but it is in these moments that we need to keep steadfast love. When we meet difficulties, we can recall the love of Jesus Christ, who was willing to give Himself up for us, even to be nailed to the cross. His love is so firm, selfless, and unconditional, and it is a love that each of us can learn and show.

So in each day of our lives, let us pursue steadfast love with faith, hope, and love. Whether in good times or hard times, we can show unwavering love by God's strength. May we, like Mary, care for others with love, be the light and salt of God, and let the world feel God's love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep recalling the love of Jesus Christ on your journey of showing steadfast love, be moved by it, and become a witness of love. Amen!
